blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】ペナルティ
blocks.translation: [RPG Creation Tutorial] Penalties

blocks.source: ペナルティとはプレイヤーの失敗に対して与えられる罰のことである。
blocks.translation: A penalty is a punishment given for a player's failure.

blocks.source: 全滅のような大きなものから、ちょっとしたコマンドミスまでペナルティは広く存在する。
blocks.translation: Penalties range from major ones, such as a party wipe, to minor command mistakes.

blocks.source: 報酬の正反対となる要素であり、ペナルティはゲーム性を実現する上で不可欠な要素である。
blocks.translation: As the opposite of rewards, penalties are an essential element in creating gameplay.

blocks.source: 「ペナルティがない」ということは「何をやっても同じ」ということであり、そこにゲーム性は存在しなくなってしまう。
blocks.translation: Having no penalties means that “everything has the same result,” causing the game to lose its gameplay.

blocks.source: また、ペナルティが大きいゲームは難易度が高いとも言われる。
blocks.translation: Games with severe penalties are also said to have a high difficulty level.

blocks.source: 目次
blocks.translation: Table of Contents

blocks.source: ペナルティの種類
blocks.translation: Types of Penalties

blocks.source: オーソドックスなＲＰＧにおけるペナルティの種類をまとめてみる。
blocks.translation: Let's take a look at the types of penalties found in traditional RPGs.

blocks.source: リソースの減少
blocks.translation: Resource Reduction

blocks.source: ＨＰ、ＭＰ、お金などのリソースの減少。
blocks.translation: The reduction of resources such as HP, MP, and money.

blocks.source: 多くの場合、これらは回復＆増加する手段が用意されている。
blocks.translation: In many cases, means of restoring and increasing these resources are provided.

blocks.source: また、アイテムの減少などもここに含めることができる。
blocks.translation: The loss of items can also be included here.

blocks.source: 大半のＲＰＧではリソースの減少は避けられない。そのため、あくまで減少を抑えるように立ち回ることになる。
blocks.translation: Resource depletion is unavoidable in most RPGs. Therefore, players must play in a way that minimizes it as much as possible.

blocks.source: やり直し
blocks.translation: Starting Over

blocks.source: 定められた地点からのやり直しを強制されるペナルティ。
blocks.translation: A penalty that forces you to start over from a designated point.

blocks.source: ダンジョンのトラップによって前のフロアに戻されたり、戦闘で全滅して戻されたり。
blocks.translation: You may be sent back to the previous floor by a dungeon trap, or sent back after being wiped out in battle.

blocks.source: 最も重要なのは、やはり全滅時のやり直しだろう。ほとんどのＲＰＧでは全員のＨＰが０になることを全滅と定義している。
blocks.translation: The most important example is probably having to start over after a party wipe. In most RPGs, a party wipe is defined as all party members' HP reaching 0.

blocks.source: そして、全滅時は直近のセーブポイント（チェックポイント）からやり直しさせられることが一般的だろう。
blocks.translation: After a party wipe, it is generally standard to restart from the most recent save point (checkpoint).

blocks.source: セーブポイントから全滅するまでのプレイは多くの場合、無駄になってしまう。残されるのはプレイヤーの経験だけとなる。
blocks.translation: In many cases, all play from the save point until the party wipe is rendered meaningless. The only thing left is the player's experience.

blocks.source: かつてはＦＦ３やペルソナ１のラストダンジョンのように２時間以上セーブできない作品もあったが、今となってはまず見られなくなった。昨今のＲＰＧでは、３０分を超えるような長時間のやり直しを強いられることは少ない。
blocks.translation: In the past, some games, such as FF3 and the final dungeon of Persona 1, did not allow you to save for more than two hours, but such games are rarely seen anymore. In modern RPGs, players are seldom forced to restart after more than 30 minutes of play.

blocks.source: またドラクエシリーズでは所持金の半減を全滅時のペナルティとする代わりに、経験値や入手したアイテムをそのまま保持してセーブポイントへ戻れるようになっている。
blocks.translation: In the Dragon Quest series, instead of halving your money as the penalty for a party wipe, you can return to a save point while retaining your experience and acquired items.

blocks.source: ※ドラクエ３ＨＤ２Ｄ版（２０２４年）では、全滅してもその戦闘からお金の減少なしでやり直しできるようになっている。驚くべきことに、低難易度では無敵となって全滅すらしない。
blocks.translation: ※In the Dragon Quest III HD-2D version (2024), even after a party wipe, you can restart the battle without losing any money. Surprisingly, on the lowest difficulty, you become invincible and cannot even suffer a party wipe.

blocks.source: 「ゲームをクリアできない」とはこのやり直しを何度も強いられることによって、先に進めなくなった状況を指すことが多い。
blocks.translation: “Being unable to clear a game” often refers to a situation in which being forced to start over repeatedly prevents you from making further progress.

blocks.source: 一般的なＲＰＧの目的は先に進むことであり、そのために全滅（＝やり直し）を避けることそのものがゲーム性の中核となっている。
blocks.translation: The goal of a typical RPG is to progress, so avoiding a party wipe (= starting over) is itself at the core of its gameplay.

blocks.source: リソースの管理を行う目的も、そもそもは全滅を避けることである。
blocks.translation: The purpose of managing resources is, in the first place, to avoid a party wipe.

blocks.source: 報酬とペナルティ
blocks.translation: Rewards and Penalties

blocks.source: ペナルティと言えば、罰金のような「罰を与えられるもの」を思い浮かべるかもしれないが、それだけではない。
blocks.translation: When you hear “penalty,” you may think of something that imposes a punishment, such as a fine, but that is not all there is to it.

blocks.source: 報酬を得られないことも事実上のペナルティである。
blocks.translation: Not receiving a reward is also effectively a penalty.

blocks.source: 例えば「今月、お前の仕事の評価低かったから給料ゼロな」と言われて怒り狂わない人はまずいないだろう。
blocks.translation: For example, hardly anyone would remain calm after being told, “Your work performance was poor this month, so you're getting no salary.”

blocks.source: 給料ゼロは給料をもらえないだけであって、罰金を払うわけではない。
blocks.translation: Getting no salary simply means not receiving a salary; it does not mean paying a fine.

blocks.source: これは給料が得られないことを自分の過去や他者の待遇と比較して、相対的にペナルティだと感じるからである。
blocks.translation: This is because people compare not receiving a salary with their past income or other people's treatment and consequently feel it is a relative penalty.

blocks.source: ソシャゲにありがちなログインボーナスは「ログインするとボーナス」であると同時に「ログインしないとペナルティ」でもあるというわけだ。
blocks.translation: The login bonuses common in social games are both “a bonus for logging in” and “a penalty for not logging in.”

blocks.source: 内心飽きてしまったゲームでも、ずるずると日課のようにログインを続けてしまい、それを重荷に感じてしまったなんて経験がある人も多いはず。
blocks.translation: Many people have probably experienced continuing to log in daily out of habit, even to a game they have secretly grown tired of, and eventually feeling that it has become a burden.

blocks.source: 最近（２０２４年）発売したＲＰＧを例に挙げてみよう。
blocks.translation: Let's take a recently released RPG (2024) as an example.

blocks.source: メタファー：リファンタジオの戦闘にはノーダメージボーナス（報酬増加）があるが、これは同時に「ダメージを受けると報酬が減るペナルティ」としても機能してしまう。
blocks.translation: Battles in Metaphor: ReFantazio feature a no-damage bonus (increased rewards), but this also functions as a penalty in which “taking damage reduces your rewards.”

blocks.source: 結果的に、以下のようなゲームデザイン上の影響が出ると考えられる。
blocks.translation: As a result, the following effects on game design can be expected.

blocks.source: 雑魚戦では防御よりも攻撃を優先したプレイスタイルが推奨される。
blocks.translation: In battles against weak enemies, a playstyle that prioritizes attacking over defending is encouraged.

blocks.source: 無理に強敵を狙うよりも確実にノーダメージ撃破できる敵を狩ったほうが効率的になる。
blocks.translation: Rather than forcing yourself to hunt powerful enemies, it is more efficient to defeat enemies you can reliably defeat without taking damage.

blocks.source: ノーダメージ撃破が苦手なライトユーザが不利になりやすい。
blocks.translation: Light users who are not good at defeating enemies without taking damage are likely to be at a disadvantage.

blocks.source: ※なお、ノーダメージボーナスを必ずしも否定しているわけではない。ノーダメージ撃破を目指すこと自体に一定のゲーム性が生まれるというメリットも存在する。
blocks.translation: ※This is not necessarily meant to reject no-damage bonuses. They also have the benefit of creating a certain degree of gameplay in the pursuit of defeating enemies without taking damage.

blocks.source: このように報酬（ボーナス）とペナルティは表と裏のような存在である。
blocks.translation: In this way, rewards (bonuses) and penalties are two sides of the same coin.

blocks.source: 報酬があるのにペナルティのないゲームは事実上存在しないと思ってもいい。
blocks.translation: You can essentially assume that no game has rewards without penalties.

blocks.source: 一般的に「失敗した者に罰を与えるよりも、成功した者に報酬を与えるほうが好ましい」とされる傾向はある。
blocks.translation: Generally, there is a tendency to believe that “rewarding those who succeed is preferable to punishing those who fail.”

blocks.source: 実際、その通りだとは思うのだが、見え方が違うだけで本質的には境界が曖昧なことには注意したい。
blocks.translation: I do think that is true, but keep in mind that the distinction is essentially ambiguous, even if the two may look different.

blocks.source: ちなみに、ユーザがペナルティに気づかないようにすること自体は可能である。
blocks.translation: Incidentally, it is possible to keep users from noticing penalties.

blocks.source: 例えば、
blocks.translation: For example,

blocks.source: 「社員全員昇給させるぞ！ ただし、お前は無能だから給料据え置きな」
blocks.translation: “I'm giving everyone a raise! However, since you're incompetent, your salary will remain unchanged.”

blocks.source: と言われたら、普通はペナルティだと感じるだろう。
blocks.translation: If you were told that, you would normally feel that it was a penalty.

blocks.source: ただ、それを通達せず、こっそり当人以外を昇給させれば、これはペナルティとして認識されなかったりする。
blocks.translation: However, if the announcement is not made and everyone except that person is quietly given a raise, it may not be recognized as a penalty.

blocks.source: 複雑なゲームシステムの作品の場合、プレイヤーが慣れるまでは隠れたペナルティに気づかないことは多い。とはいえ、狙ってゲームデザインにこれを組み込む制作者はあまりないと思うけれど……。
blocks.translation: In games with complex systems, players often do not notice hidden penalties until they become familiar with the game. That said, I doubt many creators deliberately incorporate them into their game designs...

blocks.source: ペナルティと時間
blocks.translation: Penalties and Time

blocks.source: ゲームにおけるペナルティはほとんどの場合、時間に換算できる。
blocks.translation: In most cases, penalties in games can be converted into time.

blocks.source: というのも、リアル人生とは違って、多くのゲームでは失敗は取り返しがつくように設計されているからだ。
blocks.translation: Unlike real life, this is because many games are designed so that failure can be undone.

blocks.source: もし、リアルファイトで敗北すると、滅茶苦茶痛かったり、病院送りになって治療費がかかったり、最悪死んだりする。なんなら勝利しても怪我したり、逮捕されたりする。取り返しのつかないことばかりだ。
blocks.translation: If you lose a real-life fight, it may hurt terribly, send you to the hospital with medical bills, or, at worst, get you killed. You could even get injured or arrested after winning. Almost everything that happens is irreversible.

blocks.source: けれどゲームではそんなことは起き得ない。
blocks.translation: But none of that can happen in a game.

blocks.source: 戦闘で全滅しても、ただセーブポイントからやり直せばよいだけ。ドラクエならお金を失ったりするが、それも戦闘で稼げばすぐに取り返せる程度だ。
blocks.translation: Even if your party is wiped out in battle, you only need to restart from a save point. In Dragon Quest, you may lose money, but you can quickly earn it back through battles.

blocks.source: ※対戦ゲームなどは除きます。この講座はあくまで一人で楽しむゲームを想定しています。
blocks.translation: ※This excludes competitive games and the like. This course assumes games intended to be enjoyed alone.

blocks.source: ゲーム内のキャラクターが死ぬと気分も良くないかもしれないが、自分には何の痛みもない。
blocks.translation: Having a character die in the game may not feel good, but you do not suffer any physical pain yourself.

blocks.source: 結局のところ、全滅によるペナルティとは「やり直しにかかる時間」に過ぎないとも考えられる。
blocks.translation: Ultimately, the penalty for being wiped out can be considered nothing more than the time it takes to start over.

blocks.source: 中には、ファイアーエムブレムやＦＦ６のように取り返しのつかない仲間やアイテムの消滅があったりするが、極論を言えばそれすら最初からやり直せば取り返しがついてしまう。
blocks.translation: Some games, such as Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy VI, have irreversible losses of party members or items, but in the extreme, even those can be undone by starting over from the beginning.

blocks.source: もっとも、あまりにも時間をかけすぎると究極的にはリアル人生に取り返しのつかない影響を及ぼすことも否定できない。特にネトゲやソシャゲは消費する時間も桁が違うし、時にはリアルマネーも関わったりするのでこの限りではない。
blocks.translation: Of course, if you spend far too much time playing, it cannot be denied that it may ultimately have irreversible effects on your real life. Online games and social games in particular consume vastly more time, and sometimes involve real money, so they are exceptions to this principle.

blocks.source: ゲームテンポとペナルティ
blocks.translation: Game Pacing and Penalties

blocks.source: ともあれ「ペナルティ＝時間」と考えれば、ゲームテンポ（演出時間やロード時間など）はペナルティと密接に結びつくことも分かるだろう。
blocks.translation: In any case, if you think of a “penalty = time,” you can see that game pacing (such as cutscene and loading times) is closely connected to penalties.

blocks.source: プレイヤーの勝率が同程度と仮定した場合、ボス戦が１分で終わるゲームと１０分で終わるゲームではペナルティにも差が生まれる。
blocks.translation: Assuming the player has the same win rate, there is a difference in the penalty between a game where a boss battle ends in one minute and one where it ends in ten minutes.

blocks.source: 後者のほうが格段に敗北時に無駄となる時間も長くなる。従ってペナルティが重くなる。
blocks.translation: The latter results in considerably more wasted time when you lose. Therefore, its penalty is heavier.

blocks.source: 戦闘の演出時間やロード時間の長いゲームは、当然ペナルティが増える（難易度が高い）ということでもある。
blocks.translation: Naturally, games with long battle animations or loading times also have greater penalties (and higher difficulty).

blocks.source: 一方で「１分で終わるが勝率１割のボス戦」と「５分で終わるが勝率５割のボス戦」の比較は難しい。突破できる時間の期待値は似たようなものだが、プレイヤーに与える印象は大きく異なる。
blocks.translation: On the other hand, it is difficult to compare “a boss battle that ends in one minute but has a 10% win rate” with “a boss battle that ends in five minutes but has a 50% win rate.” The expected time to win is similar, but the impression they leave on players is very different.

blocks.source: 前者のほうが勝率が低いので絶望感はあるかもしれない。プレイヤーが無理だと感じれば、投げ出す理由にもなりそうだ。あるいは逆に、緊張感があって勝つまで試行錯誤するのが面白いと感じることもありえる。
blocks.translation: The former may feel more hopeless because its win rate is lower. If players feel it is impossible, that may give them a reason to give up. Conversely, they may find the tension enjoyable and enjoy experimenting until they win.

blocks.source: どちらが良いとかではなく、この辺は制作者のセンスが問われる部分だろう。
blocks.translation: It is not a matter of which is better; this is probably an area where the creator’s sense of design is put to the test.

blocks.source: ダンジョン内でどこでもセーブできるゲームは全滅によって失う時間も短くなるので、ペナルティも下がる。
blocks.translation: In games that let you save anywhere in a dungeon, the time lost when the party is wiped out is shorter, so the penalty is also lower.

blocks.source: ※ただし、どこでもセーブはハマり（詰み）という特大のペナルティを起こす危険性があるので注意。全滅時はセーブポイントへ戻る仕組みなどと併用すればよい。
blocks.translation: ※However, be careful: saving anywhere can create the enormous penalty of getting stuck (making the game unwinnable). It can be used together with a system that returns you to a save point when your party is wiped out.

blocks.source: こういった観点から難易度が高いゲームとしては、例えばファミコンのＦＦ１～３、ＰＳのペルソナ１やレジェンドオブドラグーン、ＰＳ２のアンリミテッドサガ、Ｗｉｉのアークライズファンタジアなどが挙げられる。
blocks.translation: From this perspective, examples of difficult games include the Famicom versions of Final Fantasy I–III, Persona 1 and The Legend of Dragoon on the PlayStation, Unlimited SaGa on the PlayStation 2, and Arc Rise Fantasia on the Wii.

blocks.source: これらはセーブの機会が極端に限られたり、ボス戦に時間がかかったりするゲームである。
blocks.translation: These are games in which opportunities to save are extremely limited or boss battles take a long time.

blocks.source: 全体的に古い作品を中心に挙げたが、大きすぎるペナルティは敬遠されやすい。開発者もさすがに学習したため、近年の作品ではこういった調整は避けられる傾向にある。
blocks.translation: The examples I have given are mostly older games, but excessively large penalties tend to be avoided. Developers have learned their lesson, so recent games tend to avoid this kind of balancing.

blocks.source: サガシリーズの多くは、どこでもセーブができる上に戦闘も短期決戦寄りとなっており、ペナルティが軽い。敵は強敵揃いではあるが、これによって全体的なバランスを取っていることも分かるだろう。
blocks.translation: Most games in the SaGa series let you save anywhere, and their battles also tend to be short and decisive, making their penalties light. The enemies are certainly formidable, but you can see that this helps maintain the overall balance.

blocks.source: ゲームバランス＝ペナルティ＝ゲームテンポ
blocks.translation: Game Balance = Penalties = Game Pacing

blocks.source: もっと言ってしまうと、ゲームバランスの大部分はゲームテンポが左右する。
blocks.translation: To put it more directly, game pacing determines much of a game’s balance.

blocks.source: ゲームバランスの調整とはペナルティの調整であり、ペナルティの調整とはゲームテンポの調整なのだから、必然的にそうなってしまう。
blocks.translation: Adjusting game balance means adjusting penalties, and adjusting penalties means adjusting game pacing, so this outcome is inevitable.

blocks.source: 何度も全滅してやり直す必要があるゲームは、必然的にクリアまでの時間も長くなる。すなわちテンポが遅くなるということだ
blocks.translation: A game that requires you to be wiped out and start over repeatedly will inevitably take longer to clear. In other words, its pacing becomes slower.

blocks.source: 既に述べた通り「ゲームをクリアできない」とは、やり直しを何度も強いられることによって先に進めなくなった場合が大半である。
blocks.translation: As I mentioned earlier, in most cases, “being unable to clear a game” means being unable to progress because you are forced to start over repeatedly.

blocks.source: これが高難易度のアクションなら「自分にはクリアできない」と確信することによって、クリアを諦めることもあるだろう。
blocks.translation: If it is a highly difficult action game, you may give up on clearing it after becoming convinced that “I cannot clear this.”

blocks.source: しかし、多くのＲＰＧでは時間をかけてキャラクターを育てれば、いずれは敵に勝てるように作られており、大体誰でもエンディングに到達できるようになっている。
blocks.translation: However, most RPGs are designed so that, if you spend enough time developing your characters, you will eventually be able to defeat the enemies, allowing just about anyone to reach the ending.

blocks.source: ※たまに進行の条件（フラグ）が分からずに詰まることもあるが、現代のネット社会ではググればすぐに解決できてしまう。
blocks.translation: ※Sometimes you may get stuck because you do not know the conditions for progressing (the flag), but in today’s online society, you can quickly solve the problem by Googling it.

blocks.source: 以上より、ペナルティによってゲームクリアできない状況は現代のＲＰＧにおいて、ほとんど考えられない。
blocks.translation: Therefore, in modern RPGs, it is almost inconceivable that penalties would make it impossible to clear a game.

blocks.source: ＲＰＧは「クリアできないから諦める」のではなく「面倒臭いからやめる」のである。「これ以上、このゲームに時間をかけて先に進んでも、手間に見合った面白さを得られそうにないし、他にもっと面白いことがあるからやめる」というのが実情だろう。
blocks.translation: People do not give up on RPGs because “they cannot clear them”; they quit because “it is too much trouble.” The reality is probably that “even if I spend more time on this game and progress further, I am unlikely to get enough enjoyment to justify the effort, and there are more interesting things to do, so I will quit.”

blocks.source: このことからも、ゲームテンポ（＝時間の調整）がいかに重要なのかが分かるはずだ。
blocks.translation: This should also show how important game pacing (that is, adjusting time) is.

blocks.source: よって、ペナルティ（＝時間の消費）は行きすぎないように適切なものを設定する必要がある。
blocks.translation: Therefore, penalties (that is, time consumption) must be set appropriately so that they do not go too far.

blocks.source: 低すぎるペナルティ
blocks.translation: Penalties That Are Too Low

blocks.source: 一方で、もちろんペナルティは低すぎてもいけない。
blocks.translation: On the other hand, of course, penalties must not be too low either.

blocks.source: 演出時間とゲーム性の関連については、以下の記事でも指摘しているが理屈としては大体同じである。
blocks.translation: I also point this out in the article below regarding the relationship between presentation time and gameplay, but the reasoning is essentially the same.

blocks.source: 行き過ぎた快適性
blocks.translation: Excessive Convenience

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/500746654.html
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/500746654.html

blocks.source: 上の記事と内容が重なるが、快適性を極限まで向上させることは、ペナルティを極限まで減らすことになる。
blocks.translation: This overlaps with the article above, but maximizing convenience also means minimizing penalties.

blocks.source: 戦闘が一瞬で終わる上に全滅しても再戦が容易なゲームは、限りなく全滅がペナルティとして機能しなくなってしまう。ペナルティがないということは、ゲーム性もないということなのだ。
blocks.translation: In a game where battles end instantly and rematches are easy even after the party is wiped out, being wiped out comes close to no longer functioning as a penalty at all. Having no penalty means having no gameplay.

blocks.source: これは話を極端にしてみれば分かりやすいだろう。
blocks.translation: This becomes easier to understand if we take the idea to an extreme.

blocks.source: 戦闘を通常の１０００倍速で実行できる超快適設計。
blocks.translation: An ultra-convenient design that lets you run battles at 1,000 times the normal speed.

blocks.source: 戦闘も自動で繰り返せるので操作も必要なし。
blocks.translation: Battles can also be repeated automatically, so no input is required.

blocks.source: 全滅してもその場ですぐに復活。
blocks.translation: Even if your party is wiped out, it is immediately revived on the spot.

blocks.source: １分間放置して経験値稼ぎするだけでアッという間に適正レベルを超えてしまうことは間違いない。ボス戦も自動で戦うだけで何の問題もなく終わってしまうはず。
blocks.translation: There is no doubt that leaving the game idle for just one minute to earn experience will quickly take you beyond the appropriate level. Boss battles should also end without any trouble simply by having them fight automatically.

blocks.source: 快適性を高めただけのはずが、ゲーム性自体が完全に崩壊していることが分かるだろう。
blocks.translation: You can see that, despite merely increasing convenience, the gameplay itself has completely collapsed.

blocks.source: 演出の高速化はペナルティの低下であり、まぎれもなくゲーム性を左右する要素なのだ。
blocks.translation: Speeding up presentation effects reduces the penalties, and is unquestionably a factor that affects gameplay.

blocks.source: ファミコン版ドラクエ２は有名なＪＲＰＧとしては最も難しいと言われるが、その理由の筆頭は経験値稼ぎにかかる時間の長さにある。
blocks.translation: The Famicom version of Dragon Quest II is said to be one of the hardest well-known JRPGs, with the sheer amount of time required for grinding experience points being the primary reason.

blocks.source: 本作は通しでのテストプレイをしておらず、制作者自身が「経験値の調整に失敗した」と明言していることで有名。バグ技（いわゆる『はかぶさ』）を使わなければ、ラストダンジョン前で５～１０時間程度の経験値稼ぎを強いられる凄まじい作品だ。
blocks.translation: This game is famous for never having been playtested from beginning to end, with the creator himself explicitly stating that he “failed to balance the experience points.” Without using the glitch (commonly known as “Hakubasa”), it is an incredible game that forces you to spend roughly five to ten hours grinding experience before the final dungeon.

blocks.source: そんなドラクエ２も経験値稼ぎが１００倍速でできるならば、大して難しいと言われることもなかっただろう。
blocks.translation: Even Dragon Quest II probably would not have been considered particularly difficult if experience grinding could be done 100 times faster.

blocks.source: あくまで上記は極論だが、実際に自動戦闘や演出の高速化を極端に進めた作品はゲーム性が崩壊する危険がある。
blocks.translation: The above is merely an extreme example, but games that take automation of battles and speedups of presentation effects too far actually risk having their gameplay collapse.

blocks.source: 行き着く先はプレイヤーのやることの消滅である。やることがないなら、ゲームである必要もないのでアニメでも見ていたほうがマシ。
blocks.translation: The end result is the elimination of anything for the player to do. If there is nothing to do, it does not need to be a game at all, so you would be better off watching an anime.

blocks.source: ……というように、快適性をとことん追求した結果、無味乾燥な虚無ゲーになっていないかは気をつけたい。
blocks.translation: Thus, we should be careful that pursuing convenience to the extreme does not result in a bland, empty game.

blocks.source: ゲームがゲームであるためには、最低限の面倒臭さ（ペナルティ）は必要ということなのだと思う。
blocks.translation: I believe that games need a minimum degree of tedium (penalties) in order to remain games.

blocks.source: 心理的なペナルティ
blocks.translation: Psychological Penalties

blocks.source: 「ゲームにおけるペナルティはほとんどの場合、時間に換算できる」と述べたが、そうでないペナルティがあるとすれば、残るは心理的なものだろう。
blocks.translation: I stated that “penalties in games can, in most cases, be converted into time,” but if there are penalties that cannot, then what remains would presumably be psychological.

blocks.source: つまり「敗北した」「失敗した」「損した」「取り逃がした」という悔しさや「仲間が死んだ」という悲しさだ。
blocks.translation: In other words, the frustration of having “lost,” “failed,” “suffered a loss,” or “missed out,” and the sadness of “a companion dying.”

blocks.source: ペナルティを印象付けたい場合は、こういった要素を強調してみるのもよいだろう。敗北があってこそ、その後の勝利が際立つという側面もある。これはゲームシステムについてもストーリーについても言えることだ。
blocks.translation: If you want to make penalties leave a strong impression, emphasizing these kinds of elements may be effective. Victory feels all the more significant because there was a defeat beforehand. This applies both to game systems and to stories.

blocks.source: ただし「損した」「取り逃がした」が余りにも多く発生するゲームは嫌われる傾向にあるのでほどほどに……。
blocks.translation: However, games in which “suffering a loss” or “missing out” happens too often tend to be disliked, so moderation is advised...

blocks.source: 例えば、これまで説明してきた内容によって『限定的なレベルアップボーナス』はかなり強力なペナルティと成り得ることが分かる。
blocks.translation: For example, based on what I have explained so far, we can see that “limited level-up bonuses” can constitute a fairly powerful penalty.

blocks.source: ここで指すレベルアップボーナスは過去に以下の記事で説明している。
blocks.translation: The level-up bonuses referred to here were explained in the following article.

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/280090650.html#item2
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/280090650.html#item2

blocks.source: レベルアップボーナスは見方を変えれば「レベルアップ時にボーナスを得られないと損する」システムである。
blocks.translation: Viewed from another perspective, a level-up bonus system is one in which “you suffer a loss if you fail to receive a bonus when leveling up.”

blocks.source: 多くの作品ではレベルアップできる回数が限られているため、事実上「取り返しのつかないペナルティ」として機能してしまう。
blocks.translation: Because most games limit the number of times you can level up, this effectively functions as an “irreversible penalty.”

blocks.source: 取り戻す唯一の手段は最初からやり直すことのみ。ほとんどの作品ではクリアには何の支障もないのだが、気にする人は気にしてしまう。
blocks.translation: The only way to get it back is to start over from the beginning. In most games, it has no effect on your ability to complete the game, but some players cannot help worrying about it.

blocks.source: ボス戦限定のレアドロップなど入手機会の限定されるアイテムなども理屈上は同じである。
blocks.translation: The same applies in principle to items with limited opportunities for acquisition, such as rare drops available only from boss battles.

blocks.source: ペナルティにおいては、こういったプレイヤーの心理面も考慮していきたい。
blocks.translation: When considering penalties, I want to take these psychological aspects of the player into account as well.

blocks.source: ペナルティとゲームデザイン
blocks.translation: Penalties and Game Design

blocks.source: ペナルティは必ずしも低ければ良いというわけでもないし、高ければ良いというわけでもない。制作者の目指すべき理想や対象とするプレイヤーの層によって正解は異なる。
blocks.translation: It is not necessarily better for penalties to be low, nor is it necessarily better for them to be high. The right answer differs depending on the ideal the creator is pursuing and the type of player they are targeting.

blocks.source: 近年はゼルダの伝説ティアーズオブザキングダムのように「難易度は高く何度も死亡するが、ペナルティは低く長時間のやり直しはない」という死にゲー的なゲームデザインのヒット作も珍しくなくなった。
blocks.translation: In recent years, hit games with a punishing-game-style design, such as The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom—“the difficulty is high and you die repeatedly, but the penalties are low and there is no need to redo long stretches”—have become quite common.

blocks.source: これはヘビーユーザを満足させる一方で、ライトユーザにも最低限の配慮をするということかもしれない。
blocks.translation: Perhaps this means satisfying hardcore users while showing a minimum level of consideration for casual users as well.

blocks.source: ドラクエ３ＨＤ２ＤやＦＦ１６が過剰なぐらいライトユーザに配慮したシステムを搭載する一方で、こういった作品が強く支持されている事実は興味深い。
blocks.translation: While Dragon Quest III HD-2D and Final Fantasy XVI feature systems that seem almost excessively considerate of casual users, it is interesting that the fact that games like these are strongly supported by players.

blocks.source: ペナルティを考慮しながら、理想のゲームデザインを追求していこう。
blocks.translation: Let us pursue our ideal game design while taking penalties into consideration.

parts.source: ペナルティとゲームデザイン

lines.translation: [[LINK_1]]>Return to the RPG Creation Tutorial Index[[/LINK_1]]

texts.ペナルティとはプレイヤーの失敗に対して与えられる罰のことである。: A penalty is a punishment given for a player's failure.
texts.全滅のような大きなものから、ちょっとしたコマンドミスまでペナルティは広く存在する: Penalties range from major ones, such as a party wipe, to minor command mistakes.
texts.報酬の正反対となる要素であり、ペナルティはゲーム性を実現する上で不可欠な要素であ: As the opposite of rewards, penalties are an essential element in creating gameplay.
texts.「ペナルティがない」ということは「何をやっても同じ」ということであり、そこにゲー: Having no penalties means that “everything has the same result,” causing the game to lose its gameplay.
texts.また、ペナルティが大きいゲームは難易度が高いとも言われる。: Games with severe penalties are also said to have a high difficulty level.
texts.オーソドックスなＲＰＧにおけるペナルティの種類をまとめてみる。: Let's take a look at the types of penalties found in traditional RPGs.
texts.ＨＰ、ＭＰ、お金などのリソースの減少。: The reduction of resources such as HP, MP, and money.
texts.多くの場合、これらは回復＆増加する手段が用意されている。: In many cases, means of restoring and increasing these resources are provided.
texts.また、アイテムの減少などもここに含めることができる。: The loss of items can also be included here.
texts.大半のＲＰＧではリソースの減少は避けられない。そのため、あくまで減少を抑えるよう: Resource depletion is unavoidable in most RPGs. Therefore, players must play in a way that minimizes it as much as possible.
texts.定められた地点からのやり直しを強制されるペナルティ。: A penalty that forces you to start over from a designated point.
texts.ダンジョンのトラップによって前のフロアに戻されたり、戦闘で全滅して戻されたり。: You may be sent back to the previous floor by a dungeon trap, or sent back after being wiped out in battle.
texts.最も重要なのは、やはり全滅時のやり直しだろう。ほとんどのＲＰＧでは全員のＨＰが０: The most important example is probably having to start over after a party wipe. In most RPGs, a party wipe is defined as all party members' HP reaching 0.
texts.そして、全滅時は直近のセーブポイント（チェックポイント）からやり直しさせられるこ: After a party wipe, it is generally standard to restart from the most recent save point (checkpoint).
texts.セーブポイントから全滅するまでのプレイは多くの場合、無駄になってしまう。残される: In many cases, all play from the save point until the party wipe is rendered meaningless. The only thing left is the player's experience.
texts.かつてはＦＦ３やペルソナ１のラストダンジョンのように２時間以上セーブできない作品: In the past, some games, such as FF3 and the final dungeon of Persona 1, did not allow you to save for more than two hours, but such games are rarely seen anymore. In modern RPGs, players are seldom forced to restart after more than 30 minutes of play.
texts.またドラクエシリーズでは所持金の半減を全滅時のペナルティとする代わりに、経験値や: In the Dragon Quest series, instead of halving your money as the penalty for a party wipe, you can return to a save point while retaining your experience and acquired items.
texts.※ドラクエ３ＨＤ２Ｄ版（２０２４年）では、全滅してもその戦闘からお金の減少なしで: ※In the Dragon Quest III HD-2D version (2024), even after a party wipe, you can restart the battle without losing any money. Surprisingly, on the lowest difficulty, you become invincible and cannot even suffer a party wipe.
texts.「ゲームをクリアできない」とはこのやり直しを何度も強いられることによって、先に進: “Being unable to clear a game” often refers to a situation in which being forced to start over repeatedly prevents you from making further progress.
texts.一般的なＲＰＧの目的は先に進むことであり、そのために全滅（＝やり直し）を避けるこ: The goal of a typical RPG is to progress, so avoiding a party wipe (= starting over) is itself at the core of its gameplay.
texts.リソースの管理を行う目的も、そもそもは全滅を避けることである。: The purpose of managing resources is, in the first place, to avoid a party wipe.
texts.ペナルティと言えば、罰金のような「罰を与えられるもの」を思い浮かべるかもしれない: When you hear “penalty,” you may think of something that imposes a punishment, such as a fine, but that is not all there is to it.
texts.報酬を得られないことも事実上のペナルティである。: Not receiving a reward is also effectively a penalty.
texts.例えば「今月、お前の仕事の評価低かったから給料ゼロな」と言われて怒り狂わない人は: For example, hardly anyone would remain calm after being told, “Your work performance was poor this month, so you're getting no salary.”
texts.給料ゼロは給料をもらえないだけであって、罰金を払うわけではない。: Getting no salary simply means not receiving a salary; it does not mean paying a fine.
texts.これは給料が得られないことを自分の過去や他者の待遇と比較して、相対的にペナルティ: This is because people compare not receiving a salary with their past income or other people's treatment and consequently feel it is a relative penalty.
texts.ソシャゲにありがちなログインボーナスは「ログインするとボーナス」であると同時に「: The login bonuses common in social games are both “a bonus for logging in” and “a penalty for not logging in.”
texts.内心飽きてしまったゲームでも、ずるずると日課のようにログインを続けてしまい、それ: Many people have probably experienced continuing to log in daily out of habit, even to a game they have secretly grown tired of, and eventually feeling that it has become a burden.
texts.最近（２０２４年）発売したＲＰＧを例に挙げてみよう。: Let's take a recently released RPG (2024) as an example.
texts.メタファー：リファンタジオの戦闘にはノーダメージボーナス（報酬増加）があるが、こ: Battles in Metaphor: ReFantazio feature a no-damage bonus (increased rewards), but this also functions as a penalty in which “taking damage reduces your rewards.”
texts.結果的に、以下のようなゲームデザイン上の影響が出ると考えられる。: As a result, the following effects on game design can be expected.
texts.雑魚戦では防御よりも攻撃を優先したプレイスタイルが推奨される。: In battles against weak enemies, a playstyle that prioritizes attacking over defending is encouraged.
texts.無理に強敵を狙うよりも確実にノーダメージ撃破できる敵を狩ったほうが効率的になる。: Rather than forcing yourself to hunt powerful enemies, it is more efficient to defeat enemies you can reliably defeat without taking damage.
texts.ノーダメージ撃破が苦手なライトユーザが不利になりやすい。: Light users who are not good at defeating enemies without taking damage are likely to be at a disadvantage.
texts.※なお、ノーダメージボーナスを必ずしも否定しているわけではない。ノーダメージ撃破: ※This is not necessarily meant to reject no-damage bonuses. They also have the benefit of creating a certain degree of gameplay in the pursuit of defeating enemies without taking damage.
texts.このように報酬（ボーナス）とペナルティは表と裏のような存在である。: In this way, rewards (bonuses) and penalties are two sides of the same coin.
texts.報酬があるのにペナルティのないゲームは事実上存在しないと思ってもいい。: You can essentially assume that no game has rewards without penalties.
texts.一般的に「失敗した者に罰を与えるよりも、成功した者に報酬を与えるほうが好ましい」: Generally, there is a tendency to believe that “rewarding those who succeed is preferable to punishing those who fail.”
texts.実際、その通りだとは思うのだが、見え方が違うだけで本質的には境界が曖昧なことには: I do think that is true, but keep in mind that the distinction is essentially ambiguous, even if the two may look different.
texts.ちなみに、ユーザがペナルティに気づかないようにすること自体は可能である。: Incidentally, it is possible to keep users from noticing penalties.
texts.「社員全員昇給させるぞ！ ただし、お前は無能だから給料据え置きな」: “I'm giving everyone a raise! However, since you're incompetent, your salary will remain unchanged.”
texts.と言われたら、普通はペナルティだと感じるだろう。: If you were told that, you would normally feel that it was a penalty.
texts.ただ、それを通達せず、こっそり当人以外を昇給させれば、これはペナルティとして認識: However, if the announcement is not made and everyone except that person is quietly given a raise, it may not be recognized as a penalty.
texts.複雑なゲームシステムの作品の場合、プレイヤーが慣れるまでは隠れたペナルティに気づ: In games with complex systems, players often do not notice hidden penalties until they become familiar with the game. That said, I doubt many creators deliberately incorporate them into their game designs...
texts.ゲームにおけるペナルティはほとんどの場合、時間に換算できる。: In most cases, penalties in games can be converted into time.
texts.というのも、リアル人生とは違って、多くのゲームでは失敗は取り返しがつくように設計: Unlike real life, this is because many games are designed so that failure can be undone.
texts.もし、リアルファイトで敗北すると、滅茶苦茶痛かったり、病院送りになって治療費がか: If you lose a real-life fight, it may hurt terribly, send you to the hospital with medical bills, or, at worst, get you killed. You could even get injured or arrested after winning. Almost everything that happens is irreversible.
texts.けれどゲームではそんなことは起き得ない。: But none of that can happen in a game.
texts.戦闘で全滅しても、ただセーブポイントからやり直せばよいだけ。ドラクエならお金を失: Even if your party is wiped out in battle, you only need to restart from a save point. In Dragon Quest, you may lose money, but you can quickly earn it back through battles.
texts.※対戦ゲームなどは除きます。この講座はあくまで一人で楽しむゲームを想定しています: ※This excludes competitive games and the like. This course assumes games intended to be enjoyed alone.
texts.ゲーム内のキャラクターが死ぬと気分も良くないかもしれないが、自分には何の痛みもな: Having a character die in the game may not feel good, but you do not suffer any physical pain yourself.
texts.結局のところ、全滅によるペナルティとは「やり直しにかかる時間」に過ぎないとも考え: Ultimately, the penalty for being wiped out can be considered nothing more than the time it takes to start over.
texts.中には、ファイアーエムブレムやＦＦ６のように取り返しのつかない仲間やアイテムの消: Some games, such as Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy VI, have irreversible losses of party members or items, but in the extreme, even those can be undone by starting over from the beginning.
texts.もっとも、あまりにも時間をかけすぎると究極的にはリアル人生に取り返しのつかない影: Of course, if you spend far too much time playing, it cannot be denied that it may ultimately have irreversible effects on your real life. Online games and social games in particular consume vastly more time, and sometimes involve real money, so they are exceptions to this principle.
texts.ともあれ「ペナルティ＝時間」と考えれば、ゲームテンポ（演出時間やロード時間など）: In any case, if you think of a “penalty = time,” you can see that game pacing (such as cutscene and loading times) is closely connected to penalties.
texts.プレイヤーの勝率が同程度と仮定した場合、ボス戦が１分で終わるゲームと１０分で終わ: Assuming the player has the same win rate, there is a difference in the penalty between a game where a boss battle ends in one minute and one where it ends in ten minutes.
texts.後者のほうが格段に敗北時に無駄となる時間も長くなる。従ってペナルティが重くなる。: The latter results in considerably more wasted time when you lose. Therefore, its penalty is heavier.
texts.戦闘の演出時間やロード時間の長いゲームは、当然ペナルティが増える（難易度が高い）: Naturally, games with long battle animations or loading times also have greater penalties (and higher difficulty).
texts.一方で「１分で終わるが勝率１割のボス戦」と「５分で終わるが勝率５割のボス戦」の比: On the other hand, it is difficult to compare “a boss battle that ends in one minute but has a 10% win rate” with “a boss battle that ends in five minutes but has a 50% win rate.” The expected time to win is similar, but the impression they leave on players is very different.
texts.前者のほうが勝率が低いので絶望感はあるかもしれない。プレイヤーが無理だと感じれば: The former may feel more hopeless because its win rate is lower. If players feel it is impossible, that may give them a reason to give up. Conversely, they may find the tension enjoyable and enjoy experimenting until they win.
texts.どちらが良いとかではなく、この辺は制作者のセンスが問われる部分だろう。: It is not a matter of which is better; this is probably an area where the creator’s sense of design is put to the test.
texts.ダンジョン内でどこでもセーブできるゲームは全滅によって失う時間も短くなるので、ペ: In games that let you save anywhere in a dungeon, the time lost when the party is wiped out is shorter, so the penalty is also lower.
texts.※ただし、どこでもセーブはハマり（詰み）という特大のペナルティを起こす危険性があ: ※However, be careful: saving anywhere can create the enormous penalty of getting stuck (making the game unwinnable). It can be used together with a system that returns you to a save point when your party is wiped out.
texts.こういった観点から難易度が高いゲームとしては、例えばファミコンのＦＦ１～３、ＰＳ: From this perspective, examples of difficult games include the Famicom versions of Final Fantasy I–III, Persona 1 and The Legend of Dragoon on the PlayStation, Unlimited SaGa on the PlayStation 2, and Arc Rise Fantasia on the Wii.
texts.これらはセーブの機会が極端に限られたり、ボス戦に時間がかかったりするゲームである: These are games in which opportunities to save are extremely limited or boss battles take a long time.
texts.全体的に古い作品を中心に挙げたが、大きすぎるペナルティは敬遠されやすい。開発者も: The examples I have given are mostly older games, but excessively large penalties tend to be avoided. Developers have learned their lesson, so recent games tend to avoid this kind of balancing.

texts.これが高難易度のアクションなら「自分にはクリアできない」と確信することによって、: If it is a highly difficult action game, you may give up on clearing it after becoming convinced that “I cannot clear this.”
texts.しかし、多くのＲＰＧでは時間をかけてキャラクターを育てれば、いずれは敵に勝てるよ: However, most RPGs are designed so that, if you spend enough time developing your characters, you will eventually be able to defeat the enemies, allowing just about anyone to reach the ending.

texts.以上より、ペナルティによってゲームクリアできない状況は現代のＲＰＧにおいて、ほと: Therefore, in modern RPGs, it is almost inconceivable that penalties would make it impossible to clear a game.
texts.ＲＰＧは「クリアできないから諦める」のではなく「面倒臭いからやめる」のである。「: People do not give up on RPGs because “they cannot clear them”; they quit because “it is too much trouble.” The reality is probably that “even if I spend more time on this game and progress further, I am unlikely to get enough enjoyment to justify the effort, and there are more interesting things to do, so I will quit.”
texts.このことからも、ゲームテンポ（＝時間の調整）がいかに重要なのかが分かるはずだ。: This should also show how important game pacing (that is, adjusting time) is.
texts.よって、ペナルティ（＝時間の消費）は行きすぎないように適切なものを設定する必要が: Therefore, penalties (that is, time consumption) must be set appropriately so that they do not go too far.
texts.一方で、もちろんペナルティは低すぎてもいけない。: On the other hand, of course, penalties must not be too low either.

texts.上の記事と内容が重なるが、快適性を極限まで向上させることは、ペナルティを極限まで: This overlaps with the article above, but maximizing convenience also means minimizing penalties.
texts.戦闘が一瞬で終わる上に全滅しても再戦が容易なゲームは、限りなく全滅がペナルティと: In a game where battles end instantly and rematches are easy even after the party is wiped out, being wiped out comes close to no longer functioning as a penalty at all. Having no penalty means having no gameplay.
texts.これは話を極端にしてみれば分かりやすいだろう。: This becomes easier to understand if we take the idea to an extreme.
texts.戦闘を通常の１０００倍速で実行できる超快適設計。: An ultra-convenient design that lets you run battles at 1,000 times the normal speed.
texts.戦闘も自動で繰り返せるので操作も必要なし。: Battles can also be repeated automatically, so no input is required.
texts.全滅してもその場ですぐに復活。: Even if your party is wiped out, it is immediately revived on the spot.
texts.１分間放置して経験値稼ぎするだけでアッという間に適正レベルを超えてしまうことは間: There is no doubt that leaving the game idle for just one minute to earn experience will quickly take you beyond the appropriate level. Boss battles should also end without any trouble simply by having them fight automatically.
texts.快適性を高めただけのはずが、ゲーム性自体が完全に崩壊していることが分かるだろう。: You can see that, despite merely increasing convenience, the gameplay itself has completely collapsed.
texts.演出の高速化はペナルティの低下であり、まぎれもなくゲーム性を左右する要素なのだ。: Speeding up presentation effects reduces the penalties, and is unquestionably a factor that affects gameplay.
texts.ファミコン版ドラクエ２は有名なＪＲＰＧとしては最も難しいと言われるが、その理由の: The Famicom version of Dragon Quest II is said to be one of the hardest well-known JRPGs, with the sheer amount of time required for grinding experience points being the primary reason.
texts.本作は通しでのテストプレイをしておらず、制作者自身が「経験値の調整に失敗した」と: This game is famous for never having been playtested from beginning to end, with the creator himself explicitly stating that he “failed to balance the experience points.” Without using the glitch (commonly known as “Hakubasa”), it is an incredible game that forces you to spend roughly five to ten hours grinding experience before the final dungeon.
texts.そんなドラクエ２も経験値稼ぎが１００倍速でできるならば、大して難しいと言われるこ: Even Dragon Quest II probably would not have been considered particularly difficult if experience grinding could be done 100 times faster.
texts.あくまで上記は極論だが、実際に自動戦闘や演出の高速化を極端に進めた作品はゲーム性: The above is merely an extreme example, but games that take automation of battles and speedups of presentation effects too far actually risk having their gameplay collapse.

texts.……というように、快適性をとことん追求した結果、無味乾燥な虚無ゲーになっていない: Thus, we should be careful that pursuing convenience to the extreme does not result in a bland, empty game.
texts.ゲームがゲームであるためには、最低限の面倒臭さ（ペナルティ）は必要ということなの: I believe that games need a minimum degree of tedium (penalties) in order to remain games.
texts.「ゲームにおけるペナルティはほとんどの場合、時間に換算できる」と述べたが、そうで: I stated that “penalties in games can, in most cases, be converted into time,” but if there are penalties that cannot, then what remains would presumably be psychological.
texts.つまり「敗北した」「失敗した」「損した」「取り逃がした」という悔しさや「仲間が死: In other words, the frustration of having “lost,” “failed,” “suffered a loss,” or “missed out,” and the sadness of “a companion dying.”
texts.ペナルティを印象付けたい場合は、こういった要素を強調してみるのもよいだろう。敗北: If you want to make penalties leave a strong impression, emphasizing these kinds of elements may be effective. Victory feels all the more significant because there was a defeat beforehand. This applies both to game systems and to stories.
texts.ただし「損した」「取り逃がした」が余りにも多く発生するゲームは嫌われる傾向にある: However, games in which “suffering a loss” or “missing out” happens too often tend to be disliked, so moderation is advised...
texts.例えば、これまで説明してきた内容によって『限定的なレベルアップボーナス』はかなり: For example, based on what I have explained so far, we can see that “limited level-up bonuses” can constitute a fairly powerful penalty.

texts.多くの作品ではレベルアップできる回数が限られているため、事実上「取り返しのつかな: Because most games limit the number of times you can level up, this effectively functions as an “irreversible penalty.”
texts.取り戻す唯一の手段は最初からやり直すことのみ。ほとんどの作品ではクリアには何の支: The only way to get it back is to start over from the beginning. In most games, it has no effect on your ability to complete the game, but some players cannot help worrying about it.
texts.ボス戦限定のレアドロップなど入手機会の限定されるアイテムなども理屈上は同じである: The same applies in principle to items with limited opportunities for acquisition, such as rare drops available only from boss battles.
texts.ペナルティにおいては、こういったプレイヤーの心理面も考慮していきたい。: When considering penalties, I want to take these psychological aspects of the player into account as well.
texts.ペナルティは必ずしも低ければ良いというわけでもないし、高ければ良いというわけでも: It is not necessarily better for penalties to be low, nor is it necessarily better for them to be high. The right answer differs depending on the ideal the creator is pursuing and the type of player they are targeting.

texts.これはヘビーユーザを満足させる一方で、ライトユーザにも最低限の配慮をするというこ: Perhaps this means satisfying hardcore users while showing a minimum level of consideration for casual users as well.
